chunks: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Fuḍayl, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, the newborn and the infant do not block your inheritance and do not inherit from you, except one who has cried out loudly. And nothing that the womb has concealed, even if it moves, has any share, except that over which night and day have passed.

key_terms.آذَنَ بِالصُّرَاخِ: gave a sign by crying aloud, indicating live birth
key_terms.اخْتَلَفَ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ وَالنَّهَار: that over which night and day have passed
key_terms.يَحْجُبُكَ: prevents or blocks you in inheritance distribution

ai.seo_question: Does a newborn or unborn child inherit in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning inheritance and the status of a newborn child. It indicates that inheritance depends on live birth being established, such as by crying, and that what remains concealed in the womb does not inherit merely by movement unless it survives long enough for a clear sign of life to be recognized.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5620 - Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Indeed, a newborn or an infant does not prevent you (from inheritance) nor inherits from you unless they have cried aloud. Anything concealed in the womb, even if it moves, has no share in inheritance except what the passage of night and day might change."
